profile.name: Ishaan Chaturvedi
profile.headline: I design the systems behind the product.
profile.bio: Principal engineer on Paperly NT, a multi-tenant EdTech platform that generates verified, parametric IGCSE and IB exam questions. I care about database internals, security boundaries and architecture that holds up under real use.

systems.title: Keeping one tenant's data away from another's
systems.summary: Making isolation a property of the database, not a promise every query has to keep.
systems.problem: In a multi-tenant app, one forgotten WHERE clause leaks customer data. Trusting every query to remember the filter does not scale, and the app may resolve identity itself instead of using a managed auth layer.
systems.approach: Push the rule into Postgres with row-level security. Each request opens a transaction and sets the tenant with SET LOCAL, and the policies read that setting. I worked through the failure modes before shipping: context bleeding between pooled connections, what happens when the setting is missing, and how to roll it back.
systems.outcome: The context dies with the transaction, so a pooled connection can never carry a previous tenant's identity. A missing context fails closed.

systems.title: Enforcing plans and usage limits
systems.summary: Limits that are decided on the server and can't be bypassed from the client.
systems.problem: A SaaS with organisations, tiers and metered AI calls needs limits users cannot get around, and a record of what happened when someone disputes a charge.
systems.approach: Organisation-based tenancy with a hybrid entitlement schema: normalised columns for hard limits, JSON for feature flags. An enforcement module checks quota before any database write or LLM call, quota writes are atomic, and audit logs are append-only.
systems.outcome: Limits hold under concurrent requests, expensive calls are gated before they cost money, and every decision leaves an audit trail.

systems.title: Trusting (and not trusting) LLM output
systems.summary: Putting deterministic checks around a probabilistic model.
systems.problem: An LLM can extract structure from messy documents, but it also hallucinates fields, misaligns identifiers and sometimes contradicts the metadata it was given.
systems.approach: Treat model output as untrusted input. Ground truth comes from deterministic sources such as filenames. Sanitisers strip hallucinated fields and formatting noise, sequence and poisoning guards reject bad batches, and a reconciler aligns related documents through deterministic repair passes. Prompts are hardened against the failures seen on real documents.
systems.outcome: Model output passes verifiable gates before it is stored, so failures are caught by code and not by a person reading the result.

systems.title: Generating unlimited variants that are always valid
systems.summary: Randomness that can never produce a broken or unsolvable result.
systems.problem: Randomising numbers in a question or test case often produces ugly or unsolvable variants, such as quadratics with irrational roots when the answer should be clean.
systems.approach: Build backwards. Pick the answer first, derive the inputs from it (Vieta's formulas for quadratics), then fill the template. Computation is separated from display, a two-layer schema keeps preview text apart from the generative template, and nothing ships until an admin approves it.
systems.outcome: Every generated variant has the clean answer the template promised, and a bad template cannot reach a user.

systems.title: Making retries safe
systems.summary: Making sure a retried webhook can only ever be processed once.
systems.problem: Payment providers retry webhooks. Process the same event twice and you can fulfil an order twice, and a check-then-insert in application code leaves a race window.
systems.approach: Let the database be the lock. Insert the event against a compound unique index first, and whichever request wins the insert is the only one that processes it. Related hardening: validate uploads by magic bytes, not by trusting the file extension.
systems.outcome: Duplicate deliveries become harmless no-ops, even when two arrive at the same instant.

projects.title: Paperly NT
